selection_reasoning: This set of 4 tasks forms a coherent multi-hop chain centered around a trading/exploration sequence. The player first mines sweet berry bushes to collect sweet berries (a tradeable item and food source). Then they sell Raw Rabbit to a butcher villager to earn emeralds/currency. With trading experience established, they trade for an Emerald from another villager. Finally, they must find an orange wall banner as a landmark/reward location. The chain combines resource gathering, NPC trading mechanics, and exploration in a logical progression. The sweet berry bush mining provides initial resources and familiarity with the environment, the selling and trading tasks create a logical economic chain (sell items → earn currency → trade for specific items), and the banner finding task serves as a final exploration objective that can depend on having completed trades (the banner could be in a location revealed or accessible after trading).

edges.reason: Mining berry bushes orients player to the village area where the butcher villager is located for selling
Selling Raw Rabbit to butcher establishes trading interface familiarity needed to trade for Emerald with another villager
After completing trades, player explores further into the village to locate the orange wall banner landmark

milestones.description: Uses inventory_has because mining/harvesting sweet berry bushes drops sweet_berries into the player's inventory. The player starts with 0 sweet berries, so any berries in inventory must have come from interacting with the bushes. This is the most direct check for the mine task since the mined resource ends up in inventory.

Uses inventory_has for emerald because selling raw rabbit to the butcher villager yields an emerald. The player starts with 0 emeralds, so having ≥1 emerald proves a trade occurred. The butcher is the only source of emeralds before berries are spent (farmer requires 10 sweet berries). Combined with the dependency chain (this milestone comes after mining berries but before trading berries), emerald ≥1 reliably indicates the rabbit sale completed.

Uses inventory_has with min_count=2 because the player starts with 0 emeralds, gets 1 from selling rabbit to the butcher (milestone 2), and gets a 2nd from trading 10 sweet berries to the farmer. Since both villagers have maxUses:1, reaching 2 emeralds deterministically proves both trades occurred — the butcher trade (sell rabbit) AND the farmer trade (trade berries for emerald). There is no other emerald source in the scene.

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate/observe task. The orange wall banner is placed at spawn-relative coordinates (8, 1, -6) facing south on the oak building. The player must navigate to within 16 blocks and face toward the banner (within 60° tolerance) to demonstrate they have found and observed it. This correctly models 'player can see the target' for a find task.

scene_description: A compact village trading area with sweet berry bushes for harvesting, a butcher villager for selling raw rabbit (limited to 1 trade), a farmer villager for trading sweet berries for emeralds (limited to 1 trade), and a small oak building with an orange wall banner. The player spawns with only raw rabbit in inventory — no starting emeralds — to ensure milestones can track emerald acquisition deterministically.
task_text: Mine sweet berry bushes to collect berries, then sell Raw Rabbit to the butcher villager to earn an emerald, trade sweet berries with the farmer villager for another emerald, and finally find the orange wall banner on the small building.
design_notes: Layout: Player spawns at origin. Berry bushes at z=+2/+3 (south, 7 blocks wide, 14 total bushes). Butcher villager at ~5,0,-5 (northeast). Farmer villager at ~-5,0,-5 (northwest). Oak building at ~7-10, 0-3, -6 to -9 (far northeast) with orange wall banner facing south at ~8,1,-6 (eye level). Barrel at ~5,0,-3 and crafting table at ~6,0,-3. Player given only 16 raw rabbit (NO emeralds). Both villagers limited to maxUses:1 for deterministic milestone tracking.
